title: Create Wiki articles

text.Jak si naplánovat první týden – ukázka: How to plan your first week – demo
text.První týden ve firmě – ukázka: Your first week at the company – demo

cleanup_names: nic k mazání: recept článek nikdy neukládá (uložení posílá upozornění); EN ukázkový článek 'How to plan your first week – demo' (60746ec5-4555-4643-8891-0a89433c08b1) je trvalý předpoklad a cleanup ho nemaže – jen kontrola, že existuje

s01.narration: Want your company guides in one place where everyone finds them? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you how to create Wiki articles.

s02.narration: You'll find the Wiki in the left menu, in the Company section, under Company wiki.

s03.narration: I click Company wiki, and the article overview opens, just as employees see it.

s04.narration: Each article has its own card with a title and the dates when it was created and last updated.

s05.narration: For the Lunch menu article I click Detail, and the article opens with its attachment, here a picture of the menu.

s06.narration: Admins also get an Edit button here, but for now I'll close the window with the cross.

s07.narration: You manage articles with the Manage button at the top right, which opens a table of all articles.

s08.narration: Unlike the cards, here you also see inactive articles, and for each one its order and whether it's marked as important.

s09.narration: The Role column says who the article is for, and when it's empty, everyone can see the article.

s10.narration: I click Filters, where you can narrow the list by name, status, role or date, and I close the filters again.

s11.narration: I click Add, and the new article form opens.

s12.narration: The list of articles with a search stays on the left, so you can jump between them at any time.

s13.narration: In the Name field I type what the article is called, here How to plan your first week.

s14.narration: Employees will see the Display name above it on the card, so I type Your first week at the company.

s15.narration: Clicking the star marks the article as important, so it gets pinned to the Dashboard.

s16.narration: Article order decides where the article appears, and one means the very first spot.

s17.narration: I switch off the Active toggle, so the article stays a draft and employees won't see it yet.

s18.narration: In the editor I type the heading Your first week.

s19.narration: In the style menu, which now says Normal, I pick Heading 2, and the line becomes a heading.

s20.narration: Enter takes me to a new line, and the button with dots starts a bulleted list.

s21.narration: In the first bullet I write what awaits the newcomer on Monday.

s22.narration: Enter adds another bullet, and I write what awaits them on Tuesday.

s23.narration: The toolbar also has bold, italics, a numbered list and a list with checkboxes.

s24.narration: Other buttons insert a link, an image or a video into the text, and the last one adds an emoji.

s25.narration: Below the editor, the Select button attaches a document, spreadsheet or image, and employees will see it under the article.

s26.narration: I untick Visible to everyone, so only people with the selected role can see the article.

s27.narration: In the Role field I choose the onboarding role, so only people with this role will see the article.

s28.narration: The Save button creates the article, and Sloneek sends a notification about it right away, even when it's inactive, so only save finished text.

s29.narration: I already have the sample article saved, so I open it in the list on the left and confirm leaving the form without saving.

s30.narration: The saved article is inactive, only people with the onboarding role can see it, and the editor holds exactly what we just wrote.

s31.narration: A saved article has a chain icon next to the display name, which copies its link, for example into an onboarding task.

s32.narration: Once the article is ready, you switch on the Active toggle and click Save, but I won't save it.

s33.narration: The red Delete button removes the article, and the page will no longer be available.

s34.narration: Employees also see important articles on the Dashboard, so I click Dashboard in the menu and confirm leaving without saving.

s35.narration: Starred articles have their own tile on the Dashboard, where anyone can open them with one click.

s36.narration: Sloneek announces new articles with a notification, so in the menu I click Notifications and Integrations.

s37.narration: In the row Notification of a new post in the company Wiki, everyone sets whether they get an email, an in-app notification, or both.

s38.narration: Now you can write and format a Wiki article, choose who sees it, pin it to the Dashboard, and if anything doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s39.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
